# Value vs Growth Equities Update

Report 102 | Published 2023-01-22 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2023-1-22/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/102.json)

Style valuation and debt-ceiling liquidity.

The DCF explanation is useful, and the debt-ceiling analysis improves on prior flat-TGA assumptions. The shutdown description is factually wrong. Foreign-equity leadership failed during the named 2023 window; value also lagged badly in the disclosed interim sensitivity. Bitcoin gained over three years, while five-year pipeline and tobacco calls remain open. Broad possible-rally and bottom-retest statements are not forecast hits.

**Coverage:** All article text blocks were read. Ledger covers material macro, investment, and causal propositions; incidental descriptive statistics, boilerplate, and unreasoned position lists are excluded. Image labels were read, not image pixels.

## Claims

### 102-C01

**Liquidity affects fundamentals**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-global-debt-liquidity |
| Source blocks | 8, 9 |
| Thesis family | dollar-global-debt-liquidity |

Funding conditions affect unhedged dollar debt servicing and investment capacity. That transmission is real, but does not mean all asset prices are primarily liquidity-driven at every short horizon.

**Direction:** Supported within the defined test.

**Timing:** No numerical deadline was stated.

**Mechanism:** See rationale; this is not a forecast hit.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Global liquidity: a new phase?](https://www.bis.org/publications/qr-202312/global-liquidity-new-phase) | BIS | 2023-12-04 | Verified in the audit

Dollar-credit growth turned from +6% in Q3 2021 to -4% at end-2022; EME dollar credit fell 5% year-on-year by mid-2023, coinciding with stronger USD and tighter policy.

- [Global liquidity at September 2021](https://www.bis.org/publications/202201-commentary-ibs-gli) | BIS | Verified in the audit

Dollar credit outside the US stood at $13.4tn, including $4.2tn to emerging/developing borrowers. Currency denomination differs from lender nationality.

### 102-C04

**Shutdown is extraordinary debt measure**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | debt-ceiling-versus-shutdown |
| Source blocks | 30 |
| Thesis family | debt-ceiling-versus-shutdown |

A shutdown is triggered by an appropriations lapse, not an authorized Treasury debt-ceiling accounting measure. Delaying debt-limit payments would be a different legal and operational event. This distinction materially affects the described sequence.

**Direction:** Contradicted within the defined test.

**Timing:** No numerical deadline was stated.

**Mechanism:** See rationale; this is not a forecast hit.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Shutdowns and appropriations lapses](https://www.gao.gov/legal/appropriations-law/lapses-in-appropriations) | GAO | Verified in the audit

Government shutdowns result from expired appropriations under the Antideficiency Act, not from Treasury electing a debt-limit extraordinary measure.

- [G Fund extraordinary measures report](https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/136/Report_Operation_Status_Government_Securities_Investment_Fund_January_23_2023-June_6_2023.pdf) | US Treasury | 2023-06-29 | Verified in the audit

Bill issuance after the debt-limit agreement drew money-fund cash from ON RRP into the TGA; higher relative bill yields attracted allocations.

April 2023-November 2024 money-fund bill holdings rose roughly $1.7tn and private Treasury repo $0.9tn as ON RRP use fell about $2tn.

### 102-C07

**Recession indicators remain bearish**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | 2023 |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | indicators point toward |
| Asset or variable | 2023-us-recession |
| Source blocks | 34, 43 |

The cited leading indicators were genuinely recessionary while contemporaneous payroll and claims data were stronger. No 2023 recession followed. Official chronology identifies April 2020 as the pandemic recession trough; no 2022 recession is dated.

| Asset or variable | equity-duration-discount-rates |

For fixed positive cash flows, a longer present-value-weighted duration means greater sensitivity to the discount rate. The three toy examples illustrate that mathematical principle. Exact displayed totals depend on first-payment and growth-boundary conventions and were not independently replicated from chart pixels. Risk-free rates need not move equity discount rates one-for-one.

**Direction:** Supported within the defined test.

Value is present value of expected future cash flows at a risk-consistent discount rate; equity and enterprise cash flows require corresponding discount rates.

## Framework lessons

- A sound valuation mechanism need not time leadership.

## Verification limitations

- Captured website text is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- Chart-only numerical claims have not been visually verified.
- Selected stock/ETF adjusted-close comparisons are disclosed where used; no reconstructed portfolio backtest has been performed.
- Unresolved verdicts are not forecast failures or successes; no aggregate hit rate is inferred.
- Article body says January 23, 2023 while source metadata and URL indicate January 22; market tests conservatively start after January 23.
